description: [BEHAVIORAL] Agent pause/resume lifecycle: verify state machine correctness (active→paused_ceo→active), idempotency on pause, tenant isolation on missing agent, and persistence across page reloads.

Verify HTTP 200 response. In the response JSON, verify agent.status === 'paused_ceo' and agent.updated_at has been refreshed to a timestamp later than before.

Without navigating away from the agent detail page, verify the UI immediately reflects the new status 'paused_ceo' (or displays 'Paused'). If the UI does not auto-update, click the 'Refresh' button or reload the page and verify status is now 'paused_ceo'.

IDEMPOTENCY TEST: Click 'Pause' again (or using page.evaluate() send another PATCH to pause endpoint with the same {{agent_id}}). Verify HTTP 200 response is returned and agent.status remains 'paused_ceo'. The second pause should not change the state or error. TENANT ISOLATION TEST: Using page.evaluate(), attempt to send a PATCH request to http://localhost:3002/api/admin/command-centre/api/v1/agents/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/pause (using a fake/non-existent agent_id not belonging to the current tenant). Verify audit entries exist for the 'pause' and 'resume' actions performed in steps 4 and 7, with correct timestamps. This verifies that state changes are logged correctly across the system.

description: [BEHAVIORAL] Dashboard Metrics loads and displays accurate agent status aggregation, active brief counts, pending approvals, and department health — with stale data detection, empty-state handling, and persistence across navigation.

steps.description: Load saved superadmin session from '/home/ouroborous/code/phronex-test-runner/.tmp/comc-trunk-superadmin-state.json' using the browser storage state tool. Verify the session is active by checking no login prompt appears.

Navigate to http://localhost:3002/command-centre/dashboard. Wait for the page to fully load. Verify the page title contains 'Dashboard' or similar. Expected: Page renders without blank state (assuming org has data). Visually inspect for metric cards: look for a card showing 'Agent Count' or 'Agents', another showing 'Active Briefs', another showing 'Pending Approvals', and a 'Department Health' summary widget. If none appear, this is a BLANK_STATE failure. Check browser console for any JS errors — if errors exist, this is a CRASH failure.

Locate the agent status aggregation widget on the dashboard (typically labeled 'Agent Status' or 'By Status'). Note the displayed counts for each status category visible (e.g., 'Active: 12', 'Idle: 3', 'Paused: 1'). Record these values as {{displayed_agent_counts}}. Open the browser Developer Tools (F12) and navigate to the Network tab. Refresh the page (Ctrl+R). Filter network requests to find the GET request to '/api/v1/agents' (or similar agents endpoint). Click on it and read the JSON response body. Parse the response to extract the actual agent count breakdown by status from the backend. Store this as {{api_agent_counts}}. Compare {{displayed_agent_counts}} with {{api_agent_counts}}: the totals must match exactly. If they differ, this is a STALE_DATA failure. If the API request hangs or returns a 5xx error, this is an INTEGRATION_DOWN failure.

Open the browser DevTools Console. Type and execute: `Object.keys(localStorage).length > 0 ? 'Session data present' : 'No session'`. Verify the output indicates session data is cached. Now use page.evaluate() to make an API call: send a GET request to http://localhost:3002/api/admin/command-centre/api/v1/dashboard/metrics with the Authorization header set to the token from the current session. Capture the full JSON response. Expected: HTTP 200 with fields for 'agent_count', 'active_briefs', 'pending_approvals', and 'department_health' (or equivalent fields). Verify each field is a non-null number or object. Store the response as {{dashboard_metrics_response}}.

Navigate away from the dashboard: click on a different section (e.g., 'Briefs' link in the sidebar if present, or manually navigate to http://localhost:3002/command-centre/settings or another page). Wait 2 seconds. Then navigate back to http://localhost:3002/command-centre/dashboard. Expected: Dashboard loads again and displays the same metric values as recorded in step 2. Verify {{displayed_agent_counts}} and {{api_agent_counts}} remain consistent and no data has reverted to blank state. This tests persistence and cache validity.

Test empty-org state: Using page.evaluate(), make a GET request to http://localhost:3002/api/admin/command-centre/api/v1/dashboard/metrics with the current auth token, but append a query parameter for a test org with no data: ?org_id=test-empty-org (or use a known empty org ID if available). Alternatively, if the UI supports org-switching, switch to an empty org via the UI. Expected: The dashboard should still render without crashing. Look for empty-state messaging such as 'No agents yet', 'Get started by adding your first agent', or an onboarding CTA button like 'Add Agent' or 'Invite Team'. Verify no JS errors appear in the console. This tests MISSING_EMPTY_STATE and CRASH failure modes. Record the empty-state text as {{empty_state_messaging}}.

Return to the original dashboard (switch back to the primary org if needed). Verify the metric cards reappear with data. Cross-check the agent count displayed against the brief count: in the real business logic, briefs should have associated agents. Open DevTools and use page.evaluate() to send a GET request to http://localhost:3002/api/admin/command-centre/api/v1/briefs to retrieve the list of briefs. Count the briefs returned. Verify the 'active_briefs' metric on the dashboard matches (or is at least ≥) the count of status='active' briefs from the API. If the numbers diverge significantly, log this as a data integrity issue.

Wait 30 seconds (simulating a stale data scenario in a real-world dashboard). Manually refresh the page (Ctrl+R). Verify the metrics update correctly. If the display remains identical to the pre-refresh values and an API call was made, verify the API returned the same data (confirming no change in the backend). If the API returned different data but the UI was not updated, this is a STALE_DATA failure. Document the refresh timestamp and updated {{dashboard_metrics_response}}.

Verify the response is HTTP 404 (Not Found) or 403 (Forbidden), confirming the agent cannot be paused by a caller outside its organization. This tests TENANT_LEAK prevention.

Verify dashboard loads with metric cards (agent count, active brief count, pending approvals count, department health). Store JWT in session for subsequent API calls.

Navigate to /command-centre/approvals. Wait for approvals list to load (HTTP GET /api/v1/approvals → expect 200). Verify list is sorted by priority_score descending and contains at least 1 pending approval item with status='pending'. Click on the first pending approval (with highest priority_score) to open detail panel. Verify detail pane shows: approval id, type, summary, priority_score, cost_estimate, requesting_agent_name, impact_description, and an 'Approve' button. Record the approval.id for use in step 3.

In the approval detail panel, enter approval notes in the 'Notes' textarea field (e.g. 'Approved after review of cost impact and KPI alignment.'). Click the 'Approve' button. Expect HTTP POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}/approve with notes in request body → HTTP 200 response with updated approval object (status='approved', updated_at timestamp, approver_id set to current user id). Verify the detail panel closes and the approval no longer appears in the pending approvals list. Verify dashboard 'pending approvals count' metric decrements by 1.

Attempt to approve the same approval item again: POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}/approve with notes. Expect HTTP 409 Conflict response with error message 'Item already resolved'. Verify no duplicate approval record is created. Verify the approval status remains 'approved' in the database (query via GET /api/v1/approvals/{id} → expect status='approved'). This validates idempotency and conflict detection on resolved items.

Navigate back to /command-centre/approvals. Query the list (HTTP GET /api/v1/approvals) and verify the previously approved item is NOT in the results (pending list only). Then navigate to /command-centre/approvals?status=approved to filter by approved items. Verify the approved item appears in this filtered view with status='approved' and the notes entered in step 3 are visible in the audit_notes field. This validates persistence and filtering across page navigation.

From the approvals list, select a second pending approval item (with lower priority_score than the one in step 3). Click to open detail panel. Enter rejection notes in the 'Rejection Reason' textarea (e.g. 'Cost estimate exceeds approved budget for Q4. Recommending agent replan with lower resource allocation.'). Click the 'Reject' button. Expect HTTP POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}/reject with rejection_reason in request body → HTTP 200 response with updated approval object (status='rejected', updated_at timestamp, approver_id set to current user id). Verify the detail panel closes and the approval no longer appears in the pending list.

Validate rejection audit trail: Query GET /api/v1/approvals/{id} (rejected approval from step 6) and verify response includes status='rejected', rejection_reason matching the notes entered, approver_id, and updated_at timestamp. Cross-service integration check: verify that if the approval type is 'agent_action', the original agent proposal (in agent_proposals or decision_log table) has been marked with decision_status='rejected' and linked_approval_id set. Verify no downstream Paperclip agent execution was triggered for rejected items.

Refresh the browser (navigate to /command-centre/approvals and press F5). Verify approvals list reloads and the approved and rejected items from steps 3 and 6 do NOT appear in the pending view. Query dashboard again (navigate to /command-centre/dashboard) and verify 'pending approvals count' metric reflects the 2 items removed (decremented by 2 from initial count). This confirms persistence across session refresh and accurate metric aggregation across service boundaries.

description: [general] Comc Test_Oracles Structured Briefs — Full DEEP journey covering CRUD, validation, and persistence + cross-service integration

steps.description: Load or restore superadmin session: check for valid JWT in browser storage (localStorage key 'auth_token'). If expired or missing, navigate to /command-centre/login, enter superadmin credentials (email: superadmin@phronex.local, password from .env), click 'Sign In', wait for redirect to /command-centre/pulse. Verify session persists by checking localStorage contains non-empty 'auth_token' with exp > current timestamp.

Navigate to /command-centre/intelligence/briefs. Verify page loads with 'Structured Briefs' heading and two tabs: 'Briefs List' (active) and 'Settings'. GET /api/v1/briefs via network tab: expect HTTP 200, response is JSON array of brief objects each containing {id, created_at, content, summary}. Verify briefs are sorted descending by created_at. If no briefs exist, create one manually via POST /api/v1/briefs/send (see step 4) and return to this step.

Click 'Settings' tab within Structured Briefs. GET /api/v1/briefs/settings via network: expect HTTP 200, response contains {sections: [{name: string, enabled: boolean, order: integer}, ...], delivery_channels: [string], schedule_time: string}. Verify UI renders section toggles matching response. Default config should include at least: 'executive_summary' (enabled, order 1), 'pipeline_snapshot' (enabled, order 2), 'market_intelligence' (disabled, order 3). If settings are missing or have unexpected schema, log SCHEMA_MISMATCH failure.

In Settings tab, disable 'pipeline_snapshot' section (toggle off) and reorder 'market_intelligence' to position 2. Click 'Save Configuration' button. Network should show PUT /api/v1/briefs/settings with request body {sections: [{name: 'executive_summary', enabled: true, order: 1}, {name: 'market_intelligence', enabled: true, order: 2}, {name: 'pipeline_snapshot', enabled: false, order: 3}], delivery_channels: ['telegram', 'portal_feed'], schedule_time: '08:00'}. Expect HTTP 200 response. Verify toast notification displays 'Settings saved successfully'.

Persistence check: reload page (F5). Navigate back to /command-centre/intelligence/briefs → Settings tab. GET /api/v1/briefs/settings via network: verify response reflects saved changes (pipeline_snapshot disabled, market_intelligence at order 2). UI toggles and ordering must match persisted state. If settings reverted, log PERSISTENCE_ERROR.

Validation — attempt invalid configuration: in Settings form, try to disable 'executive_summary' section (required section). Click 'Save Configuration'. Expect HTTP 400 response with error detail 'executive_summary is a required section and cannot be disabled'. Verify error banner appears in UI with message. Confirm settings NOT saved by re-fetching GET /api/v1/briefs/settings and verifying executive_summary remains enabled.

Cross-service integration: POST /api/v1/briefs/send with force_generation=true (network tab). Expect HTTP 200 response: {id: string, status: 'processing', delivery_channels: ['telegram', 'portal_feed']}. Monitor POST /api/v1/briefs/{id} polling (max 5 attempts, 2sec intervals) until status = 'delivered'. Verify brief content in response excludes 'pipeline_snapshot' section (disabled in step 4) and includes 'market_intelligence' as section 2 (order validation). Navigate to /command-centre/intelligence/briefs/list and locate newly sent brief in table; click to expand and verify rendered brief structure matches API response sections order and enabled state.

End-to-end contract validation: confirm morning brief scheduled job (APScheduler) would use the modified settings. Check /api/v1/briefs/settings returns current config. Simulate next-day execution by calling POST /api/v1/briefs/send without force_generation, expecting brief to respect enabled sections and delivery_channels from persisted settings. Verify outbound Telegram notification (or mock via notification_log endpoint) was enqueued for both configured channels. Log success if all settings propagated correctly through the delivery pipeline; log INTEGRATION_ERROR if Telegram or portal_feed channel is missing or payload structure is malformed.

Navigate away to /command-centre/agents, perform an action (e.g. view agent details), then navigate back to /command-centre/dashboard. End-to-end session cleanup and state verification: Log out by navigating to /command-centre/logout or clearing JWT. Attempt to access /command-centre/dashboard without valid JWT and verify HTTP 401 or redirect to /command-centre/login occurs. Clear the field and re-attempt with title='Test Task' but without selecting a dept_id. Verify validation error: 'Department is required'. From the initiative detail page, click 'Invite Accountability Partner' button. Enter partner email: 'partner@acme.local', select notification preference='email_digest'. Verify all three tasks from step 3 are still present with their original due dates and department assignments. Confirm that the accountability partner invite from step 5 is still showing as 'pending' with the correct partner email.
